content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to implement an off-delay where any further pulse on the trigger input during the delay period is ignored, so that the delay time isn't extended. I've experimented with different timer options, as well as using a pulse generator and a counter, but haven't found a solution yet. The included example demonstrates that if another pulse is sent at, for instance, 4 seconds, it incorrectly adds another delay period, which I want to avoid. Any advice would be appreciated!

Hello again, I believe I've found a solution by using a latching relay. Even though this requirement seems simple, it turned out to be a bit tricky. Perhaps there's an even simpler method? For anyone facing a similar problem, please check the attachment. I'll also provide the logic schematic below.
Please try the approach shown in the attached file.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced challenges in configuring an off-delay that disregards subsequent trigger inputs during its countdown using [company_name] timer features. Although the logic is common, implementing it proved to be unintuitive, suggesting that either the product's usability or documentation could be improved for handling such scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a straightforward way to set up an off-delay timer that ignores new triggers until the current countdown finishes, without unintended extensions. They expect clear guidance or ready-made logic blocks to support this use case.
